AKBai is a mobile-first Progressive Web App (PWA) that serves as an AI-powered business operations partner for digital-first Filipino MSMEs. It communicates in Taglish through a familiar chat interface and addresses five core pillars of running a business in the Philippines: financial management, tax compliance, customer communications, daily operations, and executive decision-making.

AKBai is built specifically for the new generation of Filipino entrepreneurs who already live online but struggle with the back-office complexity of running a legitimate business. These are not traditional sari-sari store owners counting coins in a notebook. These are digitally literate sellers and creators who need help with compliance, costing, and scaling.
Online resellers, thrift shops, dropshippers. Manage orders via DMs, ship via Lalamove/J&T. Need invoicing, inventory, and help replying to floods of "HM po?" messages.
Home bakers, meal preppers, kakanin sellers. Need costing/margin calculators, order tracking, and BIR compliance as they scale past hobby level into real revenue.
Graphic designers, video editors, VAs, writers. Earn via GCash/PayPal. Need expense tracking, gross sales monitoring for 8% flat tax, and client communication polish.
2–5 person teams running social media management, events, or consulting. Need task prioritization, financial oversight, and proactive scheduling from an AI EA.

The ₱80K–₱250K/month digital-first MSME operator. These users already pay for at least one digital tool, have real compliance pain, and will pay ₱599 without hesitation. They are the sustainable revenue base and will be reached directly in Phase 1.
The ₱15K–₱80K/month operator enters via the free tier and upgrades as their business grows. Marketing should acknowledge this segment exists, but product decisions prioritize the primary persona.

All four personas are digitally comfortable (they already use Canva, CapCut, GCash daily), and are willing to pay for tools that genuinely save time. Most are non-VAT registered and use the 8% flat income tax rate. They communicate with customers primarily through Facebook Messenger, Instagram DMs, and Viber.

Traditional micro-retailers are highly price-sensitive (₱299/month is a hard sell), rarely need formal invoicing or tax tracking, and operate almost entirely in cash. They are better served by simpler tools like Packworks. AKBai’s value proposition — AI-powered compliance, communication drafting, and business intelligence — resonates with digitally native entrepreneurs who are scaling past the informal stage.

As a solo founder with a full-time corporate job, serving as your own Data Protection Officer (DPO) carries significant personal liability. AKBai will process sensitive financial and business data. Philippine law (Republic Act 10173, the Data Privacy Act of 2012) and the National Privacy Commission’s 2024 AI guidelines impose specific obligations. This section outlines the principles and compliance checklist that must be followed from day one.

Only collect what’s needed. Receipt images are processed for data extraction, then the image can be discarded (only extracted text/numbers are stored). GCash/Maya screenshots are parsed and immediately deleted after data extraction. Never collect data “just in case.”

Users can export all their data at any time (JSON/CSV download). Users can delete their account and all associated data permanently. No data is retained after deletion beyond what BIR record-keeping laws require.
All data encrypted in transit (HTTPS/TLS) and at rest (Supabase provides AES-256 encryption at rest by default). API keys and secrets stored in environment variables, never in code.

User financial data is never shared with third parties, advertisers, or partners. AI model providers (Anthropic/Claude API) process queries but do not store or train on user data per their data processing terms.
Taglish AI does not hallucinate tax advice.

All BIR-related responses include a disclaimer: “Ito ay gabay lang, hindi ito legal o tax advice. Kumonsulta sa CPA para sa mga specific na tanong.” (This is guidance only, not legal or tax advice. Consult a CPA for specific questions.)

Every OCR extraction (receipts, GCash screenshots) presents results in an editable confirmation UI before saving. AI never writes to the financial database without user approval. This protects data integrity and builds trust.
All AI-generated outputs (BIR forms, tax calculations, financial summaries) are logged with timestamps so users can review what the AI produced and when. This protects both you and the user.
As a solo founder operating this business alongside a full-time corporate role at Globe Telecom, the Data Protection Officer (DPO) obligation requires special attention:

Under NPC Circular 2016-03, you must notify both the NPC and affected data subjects within 72 hours of discovering a personal data breach involving sensitive personal information or that may cause harm. As a solo operator with a day job, you need a documented protocol that you can execute within this window regardless of your availability.

Prepare a pre-drafted NPC notification template, a pre-drafted user notification email, and a documented escalation checklist that can be triggered quickly. Store these in a secure, accessible location (not just on your dev machine).

As the user base grows past 500+ accounts, consider engaging an outsourced DPO service. This reduces personal liability and ensures professional oversight of data privacy compliance. Budget ₱5,000–₱15,000/month at scale.
You (as sole proprietor) serve as initial DPO. Register with NPC at privacy.gov.ph. Note: this carries personal liability — plan for outsourced DPO as you scale.
Register your app’s data processing systems (user accounts, financial records, AI processing) with the NPC within 20 days of launch.
Document what data you collect, why, how it’s processed, stored, shared, and secured. NPC requires PIA for all systems processing personal data.
Publish a clear, Taglish-accessible privacy policy on your website and within the app. Must cover: data collected, purpose, retention period, user rights, breach notification process.
Build features for: access requests (view my data), correction, erasure (delete my account), data portability (export). Required under DPA Section 16–18.
Prepare a process to notify NPC and affected users within 72 hours of a data breach. Pre-draft notification templates. Document escalation steps that account for your day-job constraints.
Ensure AI processing of personal data follows NPC’s Dec 2024 guidelines: transparency about AI use, human oversight for significant decisions, no automated profiling without consent.
Implement organizational (access controls, training), physical (secure hosting), and technical (encryption, logging, vulnerability scanning) safeguards per NPC minimum standards.
Administrative fines of 0.25%–2% of annual gross income, plus potential criminal liability under the DPA. The NPC has been increasingly active in enforcement since 2024. Compliance is not optional.

A full technical security architecture document (covering infrastructure hardening, penetration testing schedule, and incident response playbook) should be developed during Phase 1 build, before production launch.

Same receipt can be scanned twice (user forgets). Deduplicate by hash of amount + date + merchant ±30 min. Flag duplicates before saving, not silently reject.
When a Pro user’s payment fails, do not immediately drop them to Free. 3-day grace period with daily push notification. Supabase cron + Xendit webhook required.
Referral code system for beta invites. Track conversion from code → signup → paid. Required for word-of-mouth growth strategy in Phase 0C.
Category D — Operational Gaps (From Operations Playbook Review)

Yahoo Mail is common among target users. Supabase default SendGrid has delivery issues for PH. Requires a custom SMTP domain warmed up before launch.
Xendit webhook can fire twice on retry. Payment handler must deduplicate by payment_id before processing to prevent double-crediting subscriptions.
BIR requires sequentially numbered Official Receipts from a registered OR series. Auto-generating receipt numbers needs BIR legal sign-off before Automated Self-Invoicing ships.
Anthropic API, Supabase, Xendit, and Claude Haiku Vision (claude-haiku-3-5 Vision API) each need health checks + graceful in-app fallback messages. Set up UptimeRobot or Better Uptime.
Supabase point-in-time recovery must be explicitly enabled on the paid plan. A tested restore procedure is required before any production financial data is stored.
When session expires mid-use, show a graceful Taglish re-authentication prompt — not a raw error state or blank screen.
What happens at 2AM on a BIR deadline day when the app goes down? Solo founder needs a written protocol: detect → post status → rollback → fix. See OPS Flow 2.
Phase 0C pilot users paying ₱99–₱199 need a defined migration path when Phase 1 launches at ₱299. Define: loyalty rate, auto-upgrade path, and grandfathering period.
No App Store listing means ‘Add to Home Screen’ is non-obvious. Landing page and onboarding must include an explicit install guide step with screenshots.
Anton needs visibility into: active users, MRR, feature usage, Flag-as-Wrong queue. A Supabase dashboard + simple Retool view is sufficient for MVP.
NPC requires a defined retention period for churned users. State in Privacy Policy and enforce in system (e.g., delete transactions after 1 year of inactivity).

A 5-step hybrid onboarding experience that runs before the user accesses any product feature. AKBai learns the business, captures BIR consent, and bootstraps financial data — so that from Day 1, the Dashboard has something to show and the AI has real context to work with. This is the foundation every other feature builds on. No other Phase 1 build begins until Kilala Kita is complete.

Structured dropdowns capture categorical data before AI is involved: Business type (Online reseller / Home food seller / Freelance creative / Small agency / Other), what they sell (free text), monthly revenue range (₱<15K / ₱15K–80K / ₱80K–250K / ₱250K+), tools used today (multi-select: GCash, Maya, Shopee, Lazada, Canva, CapCut, Google Sheets, None). Data goes straight to Supabase as typed values — no hallucination risk.

AKBai asks in Taglish: “Ang iyong negosyo ba ay nakarehistro sa BIR?” Three branches: (A) Registered — ask for BIR status (8% flat / Graduated / Not sure) and full deadline opt-in. Store bir_opt_in=true. Enable Deadline Watcher + Tanong Kay BIR. (B) Not sure — KA explains the ₱250K threshold softly, one educational message, offers soft opt-in: “Gusto mo bang ipaalam ko sa iyo kapag malapit ka na sa threshold?” No pressure. (C) Not registered / Informal seller — KA acknowledges without judgment: “Walang problema — tutulungan kita sa cash flow at mga gastos mo.” Store bir_opt_in=false. Zero BIR reminders ever. One soft income threshold note only if approaching ₱250K/year. IMPORTANT: bir_opt_in boolean governs all BIR-facing features across the entire app.

AKBai asks: “Gusto kong malaman ang kasaysayan ng iyong negosyo — para mas tumpak ang aking mga sagot.” Three paths: (A) Upload existing file — user uploads CSV or XLSX (Google Sheets export or Excel). KA parses, maps to internal schema, shows preview for confirmation. Becomes the new source of truth; user stops updating the old sheet. (B) GCash/Maya screenshots — user sends screenshots of recent transactions. AI extracts and logs them via the same editable confirmation UI as Saan Napunta?. (C) Quick Start / no existing data — KA guides user through logging their very first real transaction conversationally: “Isulat mo yung pinakabagong sale o gastos mo. Anong nangyari?” One transaction logged. Warm Taglish acknowledgment. Dashboard immediately shows one data point. No blank dashboard state ever.

AKBai introduces itself in Taglish and asks 3 open-ended questions — one follow-up per question maximum. (1) “Sa normal na araw mo, ano yung pinaka-nakaka-stress?” (2) “Paano mo tinatrack yung kita at gastos mo ngayon?” (3) “Kung isa lang ang kaya kong alagaan para sa iyo — ano yung gusto mo?” Answers captured verbatim for tone-matching in future responses.
Step 5 Silent AI Synthesis (user never sees)

A second Claude API call synthesises all onboarding inputs into a structured JSON profile stored in Supabase. Profile stores: structured fields (for reliable logic), verbatim quotes (for tone-matching), bir_opt_in boolean (governs all BIR features), data_source type (upload / gcash / quickstart), and a baseline financial snapshot from the bootstrap data. Injected into every subsequent system prompt, scoped strictly to this user’s auth.uid(). Profile updates over time: 10+ transactions logged, repeated BIR questions, revenue crossing a band threshold.

All four layers must be in place before any user data is stored in production. This is a hard launch gate — not a nice-to-have. One misconfigured RLS policy exposing User A’s financial data to User B is an NPC-reportable breach on Day 1.
Every table storing user context enforces RLS with auth.uid() = user_id. Tables: business_profiles, conversations, transactions, reminders. Verified in the Phase 1 RLS audit before launch.

Every Claude API call assembles the system prompt server-side, never on the client. Four blocks: (1) Core KA Persona — shared identity, Taglish style, disclaimer rules. (2) User Context — business profile fetched by auth.uid(). (3) Conversation History — last N messages for this user only. (4) Current Message — unique per session.
Conversation history is stored and fetched per user_id. A global log is never passed to Claude. Each session only ever sees its own user’s history.
Business profile updates over time, incrementing profile_version. Triggers: 10+ transactions, repeated BIR questions, voice usage patterns, revenue crossing a band threshold.

This section defines the brand identity, UI/UX philosophy, and phased marketing execution for AKBai. As a solo founder competing against funded tools and generic AI, your differentiation is not features — it’s the depth of Filipino context, the warmth of the brand, and the parasocial trust you build with your audience before anyone pays a single peso.

The AI partner should never be positioned as a bot, a tool, or an assistant. It is a Katuwang — a Filipino word meaning “partner” or “co-worker”, connoting equal footing and genuine collaboration. This framing is intentional:
It knows your numbers, your deadlines, your customers. It never asks you to repeat yourself.
Taglish-speaking, never condescending. Calls users by name. Uses “po” appropriately but not excessively. Feels like a bright colleague, not a corporate chatbot.
The Katuwang speaks first. It surfaces problems before users ask. Morning Briefings, deadline alerts, cash flow warnings — initiated by the AI, not triggered by the user.
Zero unsolicited promotions, upsell nags, or engagement-bait notifications. Every notification must have genuine informational value. If it doesn’t help the user’s business, it doesn’t get sent.

The interface is not a traditional dashboard and not a pure chatbot. It is a Chat + Card hybrid: users input via natural language or voice, the AI outputs rich, editable UI cards rather than walls of text.
Vendor, amount, date, category. Editable fields highlighted in yellow for low-confidence OCR. Confirm / Edit buttons.
A wall of text saying "I extracted ₱245 from SM Supermarket on March 3" is easy to misread. A card is scannable in 2 seconds.
3–5 priority items. Color-coded urgency (red = urgent, green = OK). Tap to expand any item.
Users open the app 30 seconds before a delivery. Cards let them process info at a glance, not read paragraphs.
Form name, due date, estimated amount, countdown. "File Now" button with eBIRForms cheat sheet link.
Urgency is visual. A red countdown badge on a card triggers action better than a text reminder.
Client name, amount, due date, payment status pill (Paid/Pending/Overdue). Tap to resend or mark paid.
Invoice management needs structure. A card makes it actionable without navigating to a separate screen.
Product name, cost breakdown table, suggested retail at 30/50/100% margin. Editable.

The following three positions emerged from investor Q&A review. They are not feature refinements — they are strategic stances that must be reflected in how the product is built, prioritised, and communicated from Phase 1 onward.
The One Thing: Clarity as Core Value Proposition

The roadmap describes AKBai across five pillars with equal weight. This is a product architecture decision, not a positioning decision. The pitch, the onboarding, the marketing, and the first user experience must all orbit a single emotional core:
AKBai tells Filipino sellers the truth about their business — in their language, before it’s too late to do anything about it. Everything else is infrastructure for that moment.
Rebuild the pitch around this single truth:
The features exist quietly in service of the clarity moment. Lead with the emotional problem, not the solution set.
Design the Maria Moment as the product north star:

Maria the home baker opens KA and sees: “Kumikita ka. ₱18,400 ang net mo this month. Pero pag tinignan natin ang butter costs, may paraan para dagdagan pa iyan.” This moment — where AKBai tells the user something true about their business they didn’t know — must happen within the first 7 days for every user. Design backwards from it. Every feature decision in every phase should be evaluated against one question: does this get users to their Maria Moment faster or more reliably?
Evaluate every feature against three filters:
Does it deepen business context? Does it reinforce Filipino-specific soul? Does it increase switching cost? Features that do none of these are deprioritised regardless of how appealing they are.

The moat is not features. Features get copied by ChatGenie, Taxumo, or a well-resourced new entrant within 6 months. The real moat is three compounding layers that become harder to replicate the longer a user stays active:
Every receipt scanned, every BIR deadline tracked, every transaction logged builds a picture of the user’s business that no generic tool has. Switching to ChatGPT means starting from zero.
Grows every day a user is active

Built specifically for Filipino sellers — not adapted from a Western product. The Taglish voice, the BIR-specific logic, the GCash-native workflows. Competitors can copy features; they cannot copy 12 months of Filipino-specific product decisions.

A user with 18 months of receipts, tax history, and business profile inside KA faces a complete data migration to leave. The longer they stay, the higher the cost of leaving — not through lock-in, but through genuine accumulated value.

⚠️ The window is 12–18 months. This is the realistic timeline before a well-resourced competitor ships a credible Taglish AI business tool. Speed to 500 deeply engaged users matters more than breadth of features. Get users to daily active usage fast — the moat builds itself from there.
Claude API Dependency: Honest Position & Mitigation
This is a real structural risk. The honest position is that the dependency is the right tradeoff at this stage — but it must be managed consciously, not ignored.
The dependency is correct for now:

Building a competitive AI reasoning layer from scratch is not feasible for a solo founder. Anthropic’s data processing terms currently protect user data. The quality advantage for Taglish reasoning and structured extraction is real. Accept the dependency; manage the risk.
The moat is not the AI — it is everything around it:

User data, business profiles, the Taglish prompt corpus, the Filipino-specific BIR logic, the Katuwang brand trust. If Anthropic raises prices or changes terms, those assets survive. The AI layer is replaceable; the accumulated user context is not.

(1) If Anthropic raises API pricing by more than 30%, run a margin stress test immediately. (2) If Anthropic changes data processing terms in ways that affect NPC compliance, engage a lawyer within 30 days. (3) If a materially better model for Taglish reasoning becomes available from another provider, evaluate migration within 90 days. None of these are crises — they are business decisions that require a clear head.
Provider diversification is a Phase 3 consideration:

Do not architect for multi-provider AI now — it adds complexity that will slow you down at a stage where speed matters most. Revisit at Phase 3 if the dependency has become a material commercial risk.

Your exposure is real but not unique. The mitigation is margin discipline from Day 1: know your per-user AI cost, build the circuit breaker, and price with headroom.
